title: Effects of Josephson Junction Non-idealities on Adiabatic Quantum Flux Parametron Circuits
authors: Daryoush Shiri, Likai Yang, Mohamed A. Hassan, Philip Krantz, Eric T. Holland
abstract: Adiabatic quantum flux parametron (AQFP) gate is a promising approach to scale up the cryogenic microwave electronics for superconducting qubit multiplexed control. However, the performance of these circuits depends on the quality of the Josephson junctions which are ideally superconductor-insulator-superconductor (SIS) type following the ideal sinusoidal relation between current and quantum phase. We demonstrate how the non-sinusoidal current-phase relation in Superconductor-Normal metal-Superconductor (SNS) and weak link (WL) junctions affects the speed, delay, and margin of the AQFP gates. The JJ models are defined in the Keysight ADS simulator using symbolically defined device (SDD) method.
summary: This paper analyzes the performance of Adiabatic Quantum Flux Parametron gates, crucial for cryogenic superconducting electronics. It models how non-ideal Josephson junctions (SNS and WL) deviate from ideal sinusoidal behavior by using polynomial expansions in circuit simulations. The results quantify these deviations, showing that junction type dictates critical trade-offs between switching speed, current swing, and operational margin.
main_problem: The study investigates how non-sinusoidal current-phase relations (CPR) in Josephson junctions affect the performance of Adiabatic Quantum Flux Parametron (AQFP) gates.
main_result: Non-ideal junction types (SNS and WL) significantly alter the switching dynamics, delay, and stability margins compared to ideal SIS junctions, demonstrating trade-offs between speed and current swing for cryogenic digital processing.
method: The authors used symbolic device modeling within the Keysight ADS simulator to analyze transient behavior of AQFP circuits under various junction models.
model_or_system: The system is based on AQFP logic gates, superconducting circuits utilizing SQUID loops containing Josephson Junctions (JJ). The model compares ideal SIS junctions against non-ideal SNS and WL junctions by incorporating their respective CPRs into the circuit simulation.
key_observables: Switching speed, delay, output current swing ($\mu$A), and signal integrity in a 3-stage shift register.
important_parameters: Critical currents ($I_{c1} = I_{c2} = 50\ \mu	ext{A}$), operating frequency (e.g., $5 	ext{ GHz}$), and the nature of the CPR deviation from sinusoidal.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that using polynomial models via SDD accurately captures the behavior of non-ideal junctions for circuit simulation purposes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the AQFP buffer schematic, potential energy profiles, comparisons of $I-\phi$ curves (SIS vs. SNS vs. WL), and transient simulations showing signal propagation through a 3-stage shift register.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the AQFP concept using ideal junctions, then models non-ideal junctions (SNS/WL) via polynomial expansions, simulates the basic buffer gate operation, and finally demonstrates functionality using a multi-stage shift register.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses hardware limitations in superconducting quantum computing by analyzing how material imperfections (non-sinusoidal CPRs) impact fundamental logic gate performance metrics like speed and energy dissipation.
